purpose: Separate baseline imbalance, motion adjustment, and individual influence on the SUDMEX FPN gateway contrast; assess NuMIT applicability.
cohort: The same 40 complete T0/T1 pairs, 22 active and 18 sham; no new exclusions
uncertainty: OLS coefficients with HC3 and t intervals consistently across the five models; original Welch result retained as reference
diagnostics: Arm means, SDs, baseline standardized differences, baseline/followup overlap and correlations
Algebraic decomposition of raw-to-adjusted coefficient change using joint-model covariate coefficients times observed arm imbalances; not a causal mediation decomposition
Leave-one-participant-out fits for all five models, Cook distance and leverage; no participant deletion from the reported full-cohort estimates
5000 stratified participant bootstrap replicates for the four core model coefficients
Baseline-adjusted HC3 treatment comparisons for all seven clinical outcomes, one BH family; clinical source flags remain unchanged
normalization_assessment: Read supplied NuMIT paper and original implementation; distinguish PID demonstration from the proposed PhiID extension
Read only pure local mathematical helper functions; do not execute old cohort drivers or reanalyse private data
Audit Gaussian time-delayed mutual information and autocorrelation at the fixed production lag in TMS acute scans, with solver parity checks against completed matrices
Bounded method-validation pilot if justified: fixed seed, held-out synthetic null calibration, TMI matching, finite-sample and quantile saturation checks; no full normalized treatment-effect search
interpretation: Do not rebrand these diagnostics as preregistered, replace the completed primary result, select models for significance, or infer causation from baseline-change correlations. NuMIT cannot correct arm imbalance or head motion.
